description: Work out federal overtime pay for one workweek of a non-exempt employee under the Fair Labor Standards Act. Send the hours worked as pay lines (hours at an hourly rate, or hours paid a flat sum such as piece-rate, day-rate or job-rate earnings) and any other pay that belongs in the regular rate for that week (non-discretionary bonus, commission, shift premium). Get back the regular rate (all such pay divided by all hours worked), the overtime hours over 40, the half-time overtime premium, any federal minimum wage shortfall, and the total due for the week; send amount_paid to see whether the week was paid in full. Federal rule only; state overtime rules differ. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/flsa-overtime). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

amount_paid.description: Optional: what was actually paid for the week (straight time plus any overtime pay), to check it against the amount due.

label.description: Optional label for the week, e.g. 'week ending 2026-03-14 crew B' (your own text, echoed; not a person's name).

lines.description: Hours actually worked in the one workweek (1 to 50 lines). Each line: hours, and either hourly_rate or earnings (a flat sum for those hours: piece-rate, day-rate or job-rate pay).

earnings.description: Flat straight-time pay for these hours: piece-rate, day-rate or job-rate earnings. Send this or hourly_rate.

hourly_rate.description: Straight-time hourly rate for these hours (up to 4 decimals). Send this or earnings.

hours.description: Hours actually worked on this line (up to 2 decimals). Paid leave, holidays not worked and other hours not worked do not belong here.

other_pay.description: Other pay for this workweek that belongs in the regular rate (up to 20). Leave out discretionary bonuses, gifts, expense reimbursements, pay for hours not worked and overtime premiums (29 U.S.C. 207(e)).

amount.description: Amount earned in, or allocated to, this workweek. For a bonus or commission covering several weeks, send this week's share (29 CFR 778.209(b): an equal share per week when it cannot be tied to weeks).

kind.description: What the pay is (shown back; every kind is added to the regular rate the same way).
